top_signal.title: How do you start small when you have family connections in a technical industry?
top_signal.summary: I'm finishing a master's in business in New Zealand and starting to explore a small venture connected to my family's work. My dad works in the fiber industry in China, and through him I can speak with suppliers of high-performance fibers such as UHMWPE, LCP and PTFE. Our family's experience is mainly on the B2B side, and I'm still learning the technical details myself.   What interests me about these materials is the possibility of improving fairly ordinary products: making something last longer, reducing its weight, or helping it cope with demanding conditions. The more I look into it, the more questions I have about processing, cost and whether an improvement would actually matter to the person using it.   One small idea I've been exploring is using UHMWPE in the high-wear areas of socks. I also know someone working in sock manufacturing, so there are people I can ask questions. It's still an early idea, with no tested product yet. Comfort, manufacturing compatibility and the extra cost all need figuring out.   My dad's advice has been to understand demand first and then work out the product. That makes sense to me, and I'm trying to work out a manageable first step with limited money and experience. I'm also open to learning through a small B2B project as I get to understand the industry.
